performance.title: OCR performance
performance.autoHint: In automatic mode, at least half of the cores are kept free (recommended: {{recommended}} of {{cpu}}).
performance.manualHint: In manual mode, you choose how many pages are processed at the same time.
performance.gpuCapHint: Capped at {{cap}} concurrent pages on this machine: every page in flight holds GPU memory ({{vram}} GB VRAM). Beyond that the card spills into system memory and everything slows down badly. The {{cpu}} cores are only fully usable without a GPU. Larger scans lower this cap further.
performance.allCoresWarning: All cores will be used — the PC may become sluggish during OCR.
performance.coresBusy: About {{effective}} core(s) busy, ~{{free}} left free to use the PC.
performance.moreWorkers: More workers = faster, but more cores and VRAM used.
performance.threadsHint: Keep it at 1: too many threads × workers saturates the CPU and slows everything down.
performance.poolThresholdHint: Below this number of pages, OCR stays sequential (starting the pool isn't worth it).

indexing.title: Indexing performance
indexing.description: Building an index reads and parses the XML produced by the OCR. That work is spread over several processes; it does not use the GPU.
indexing.workersHint: XML files read in parallel (recommended: {{recommended}} of {{cpu}}). Past a few concurrent reads it is the network share that limits, not the CPU.
indexing.thresholdHint: Below this number of files, indexing stays sequential (starting the processes is not worth it).

machine.title: This computer
machine.description: Identifies this PC so that, on the Tasks page, you can tell apart the OCR and indexing jobs launched from each machine. This information is stored locally on this PC (never on the shared NAS).
